title: How are you guys animating your combat animations?
author: W3103_
selftext:
Total hobbyist and amateur here

Some of your guys combat animations are so epic, im jealous 

I don’t know how to code, so most of my game dev so far has been prompting Claude with what I want, but no matter what I describe, Claude’s animations, for my models in the 3D game I’m working on, are very basic and average 

How do you animate them with ai? What tools/workflows are you using ? 

I’m literally after very basic, slashing with claws and boxing/striking animations - but I hate everything it iterates for me and I’m at a loss 

Thanks guys pls don’t roast me for being dumb 🫡

comments.author: bellmelbon
comments.body: You need reference posing , use thess key word impactframe , hit feedback , weighted animation

replies.author: BIGCHUG1404
replies.body: \^ if you are vibe coding then language and visuals are your toolbox. Using the jargon like the above mentions as well as picture evidence (I edit screenshots in paint).

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body: Right now AI makes shitty animations. You get better results by filming yourself on a phone and using as a reference for keyframes

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body: Im actually mostly animating by myself in Autodesk Maya. I do use Motionmaker that is a AI motion tool inside of Maya but its not doing complex animation for me. Where AI helped me a lot tho is the technical (art) side of animation. I use an add on called mGear for Maya for example and its a rigging framework that allows a lot of stuff and also has rigging presets. With Claude i have built custom tools and presets that made the rigging part a better experience like the one click rig rebuild. I will also work on some more ambitios custom tools for the animation/rigging part of the work like the "creature rig factory" and "deformation inspector" that will take me weeks to make and get polished for production. Also Motionmaker is now trainable on custom data so i have yet to see if Claude can work wonders with this one too.

comments.author: Toastti
comments.body:
The answer is don't animate them with Claude in 3d. You want to [Mixamo](https://www.mixamo.com/#/) this has a massive amount of FREE mocap animations. So it looks realistic as they had actual humans do the movements and recorded them.

If you use AI to create the actual animation you are going to get something very stiff and awkward. I'm sure In a year or two they will be capable of this. But not today

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: I’ve been using Mixamo, it’s fantastic

replies.author: futuneral
replies.body: Why not both? Claude is quite good at "take this mixamo attack animation but make the sword swing wider."

comments.author: jivenossauro
comments.body: Avoid doing the full animation yourself with AI. Instead, ask claude to find where you should get animations from. Theres many offered for free that can be used commercially

comments.author: PulIthEld
comments.body: Mixamo and i bought a pack of animations from the unity store

comments.author: Ok-Leading8654
comments.body: I've found [sam-3d-body-dinov3](https://huggingface.co/facebook/sam-3d-body-dinov3) to be very decent, it requires some cleanup in blender, but claude can do that for you, and you get to film your own animations! It does require running the AI on your own machine, but heck, I got it working on a 1070 with no trouble at all.

comments.author: guanzo91
comments.body: I learned recently that Quest 3 can perform decent mocap of the torso and up, so arms, fingers, neck, head, etc. Legs are a best effort guess though. I tested it out and it's quite decent for a budget mocap setup.
